summary_html: Agency makes a **substantiated (founded)** finding of abuse/neglect. This decision often unlocks **court petitions**, **service mandates**, and **federal reporting** duties.

primary_citations.citation_text: Maryland - Md. Code, Family Law Article §§ 5-701 et seq. (Child Abuse and Neglect; definitions at § 5-701, mandatory reporting at §§ 5-704 and 5-705, investigation at § 5-706, appeal of findings at § 5-706.1)
Maryland - Courts & Judicial Proc. § 3-801 et seq. (CINA—Child in Need of Assistance proceedings)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: B.H. v. Anne Arundel County Department of Social Services
key_cases.court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an administrative law judge's decision upholding a finding of indicated child abuse, holding that a mixed question of law and fact in such an appeal is reviewed under the substantial evidence test.
key_cases.relevance: It states the standard of review that governs a parent's administrative challenge to an indicated finding under FL § 5-706.1.
key_cases.quote: When the agency decision being judicially reviewed is a mixed question of law and fact, the reviewing court applies the substantial evidence test.

key_cases.case_name: Department of Human Resources v. Cosby
key_cases.court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
key_cases.holding: The court held that collateral estoppel may be raised and applied in an FL § 5-706.1 appeal hearing, so an ALJ properly dismissed the appeal of an indicated finding already litigated in the CINA case.
key_cases.relevance: It controls the preclusive effect of a CINA adjudication on a parent's separate administrative appeal of an indicated finding.
key_cases.quote: we hold that the doctrine of collateral estoppel may be raised and applied in a F.L. § 5-706.1 hearing

key_cases.case_name: Montgomery County Department of Health & Human Services v. P.F.
key_cases.court: Court of Special Appeals of Maryland
key_cases.holding: The court affirmed an order requiring the agency to reclassify a sexual-abuse finding as 'ruled out' and to expunge its records and central registry entry, where the ALJ found no credible evidence that abuse occurred after a deficient investigation.
key_cases.relevance: It shows that an indicated or unsubstantiated finding can be overturned and stricken when the investigation is unsound.
key_cases.quote: MCHHS must comply with the order to reclassify the case as "ruled out," and expunge its records and registry.

key_cases.case_name: Hodge ex rel. Hodge v. Jones
key_cases.court: United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit
key_cases.holding: The court held that Maryland's confidential retention of an 'unsubstantiated' and 'ruled out' child-abuse investigation file did not violate the family's constitutional privacy, familial or due process rights, because there was no cognizable stigma and no loss of a tangible interest.
key_cases.relevance: It defines the constitutional limits on challenging record retention following an abuse investigation.
key_cases.quote: a conclusory allegation of reputational injury which, absent a cognizable stigma and the ensuing loss of a tangible interest, fails to state a cause of action under Sec. 1983

key_cases.case_name: McClanahan v. Washington County Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: Reversing the Court of Special Appeals and remanding to the ALJ, the Court held that a person may be placed on the DHR central registry as responsible for child abuse — including abuse by mental injury — only if the person intended to injure the child or acted in reckless disregard of the child's welfare.
key_cases.relevance: It supplies the scienter element Maryland requires before an agency may make an indicated abuse finding, and it corrects the contrary intermediate-appellate rule the earlier brief relied on.
key_cases.quote: inclusion on the central registry as a child abuser is not permitted unless Mother intended to harm R or acted in reckless disregard of R's welfare

key_cases.case_name: Taylor v. Harford County Department of Social Services
key_cases.holding: The Court vacated an ALJ's finding of 'indicated' child physical abuse, holding that the ALJ erred by using tort foreseeability to infer intent and that an intentional act causing unintended injury supports an indicated finding only if the act was reckless or deliberately intended to harm the child.
key_cases.relevance: Taylor is the Court of Appeals' controlling decision on what an agency must establish to sustain an 'indicated' child abuse finding, and it is the source of the scienter rule McClanahan later extended.
key_cases.quote: We hold that, under the circumstances here present, the intentional act must be shown to have been either reckless in its nature or deliberately intended to harm the child
